title: Lag, rebalances, retention, and the debugging checklist
outcome: Diagnose slow or missing processing from broker, group, DB, and event identity evidence.
drawbacks: Metrics and retained history have limits; reset/replay can affect business effects.

trace.title: Event identity
trace.detail: Lag is a progress difference, not a complete user-impact measure. A small lag can contain very old important work; a large lag can drain quickly. Observe oldest unprocessed age, processing rate, errors/retries, and backlog growth as well.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Missing report → locate outbox event → publication result → topic/partition record → group committed progress → inbox row → projection. The first missing boundary narrows the investigation.

For slow work, compare producer rate, consumer processing time, DB wait, hot partitions, and rebalance frequency. Adding partitions/consumers changes contracts and is not always the smallest repair.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: A group may be subscribed to the wrong topic or have a different ID. earliest does not rewind existing commits. Resetting offsets can repeat external effects.

recallPrompt: Without notes: Diagnose slow or missing processing from broker, group, DB, and event identity evidence. Explain one example and one failure.
